newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on mild weather, wheat slide.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on mild weather, wheat slide.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on U.S. Midwest weather that was considered nearly ideal for corn production and on a drop in wheat futures, traders said.
Corn dealings were dull and a mildly bearish tone was evident despite supportive influence from export news and a USDA Supply/Demand Report that was neutral to the market.

USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of old crop corn during the week ended June 5 totaled 626,200 tonnes, above expectaqtions for 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes. New crop sales totaled 474,900 tonnes, above expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
The government also pegged 1996-97 U.S. corn carryout at 909 million bushels, the same as the 909 million predicted by USDA in its May supply/demand report.
SAK Futures sold five million bushels of July, Cargill Inc sold one million July and sold two million December, traders said.
Refco Inc bought three million bushels of December and SAK bought 1.5 million December as did ING Derivatives, traders said.
Corn closed one to two cents per bushel lower, with July down 1-1/4 at $2.71-1/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 40,000 contracts, below the 45,799 traded Wednesday.

In corn options, USA Trading bought 1,000 September $2.20 puts at 3/4 cent, ING Derivatives bought 500 July $2.70 puts at 2-2-1/4 cents, LIT America bought 500 July $3.10 calls at 1/8 cent and FIMAT Futures sold 400 December $2.70 calls at nine to 10 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, above the 10,563 traded Wednesday.
